features.title: Automatic feature branch creation tied to OpenSpec
features.description: When a spec change is detected (new version or x-spec-id in openapi.yaml), automatically create a git branch feature/<service>-<spec-id> before generating artifacts.
features.motivation: Isolate each spec iteration in its own branch, making it traceable from OpenSpec change to git history.

branchNaming.optionA: feature/<service>-spec-v<info.version> — derived from semver in openapi.yaml info block
branchNaming.optionB: feature/<service>-<x-spec-id> — derived from a custom x-spec-id extension field in openapi.yaml info block (preferred: more semantic)

implementation.specIdResolution: Read info.x-spec-id (or info.version fallback) from libs/<service>/specs/openapi.yaml
implementation.changeDetection: Compare openapi.yaml info.version against microservice.json specVersion field

features.title: Spec scope guard — prevent modifications outside service boundary
features.description: A new check:spec-scope command validates that all modified files (git diff --name-only HEAD) are within libs/<service>/ when working on a feature branch for that service.
features.motivation: Enforce the SDD contract: a spec change should only affect the files it declares it generates or modifies.

conditionallyAllowed: libs/shared/ — allowed if the service explicitly declares a shared dependency
forbidden: apps/api/src/app.module.ts (unless it is a new service registration)
design.triggerPoint: scripts/workflows/index.ts verify() — after existing validation gates

features.title: Production log shipping and transports
features.description: Track the production logging readiness checklist and evaluate production destinations for Pino logs after the deployment and observability platform is selected. The structured-logging change keeps production output as JSON on stdout and uses pino-pretty only in development.
features.motivation: Route operational logs to an appropriate collector or managed destination with deliberate retention, resilience, security, and cost controls instead of coupling the API to an unselected vendor.

considerations: Select the production collector and destination based on the deployment platform.
Use Pino transports in worker threads for log processing that could block the API event loop.
Define delivery failure, buffering, backpressure, retry, and shutdown behavior.
Preserve redaction before logs leave the process and define retention and volume limits.
Keep stdout JSON available for local operation and platform-native collection.

productionReadinessChecklist.item: Control levels with LOG_LEVEL; default to warn in production and info outside production.
Use pino-pretty only in development and raw JSON in production.
Limit external destinations to warn/error and configure production transports.
Review high-volume paths to avoid per-item logging in loops and sample noisy health checks where appropriate.
Never log request or response bodies.
Redact credentials, tokens, passwords, card numbers, security codes, and sensitive headers with serialized-output regression tests.
Serialize exceptions under err rather than logging err.message alone.
Use child loggers for API modules and requests; add job context when background jobs are introduced.
Set service and environment base fields; add build/version metadata when its source is defined.
Configure multiple production destinations such as file and external monitoring only after deployment requirements are known.
Keep logger configuration in a dedicated host configuration file registered once by AppModule.

updatedPipeline: openapi.yaml edited with new version or x-spec-id
pnpm propose → detect spec change → git checkout -b feature/<service>-<spec-id> → generateFromSpec()
pnpm commit_flow → guard: assert current branch matches feature/* pattern

openQuestions: Use x-spec-id extension field in openapi.yaml (optionB) or derive branch name from semver (optionA)?
Should libs/shared/ changes be allowed within a spec scope without explicit declaration?
Should commit_flow hard-fail if not on a feature/* branch, or just warn?
